sentences.text: This is GLEAMM, a microgrid laboratory ten miles west of Texas Tech in Lubbock.
Since 2015, it has given REPACSS its building, its power, and dense instrumentation and control.
Its main renewable source is a 350 kilowatt solar array, right beside the machine room.
Next to it sit a 550 kilowatt-hour battery, a 500 kilowatt diesel generator, and the commercial grid.
Nearby wind turbines feed the utility grid, so grid power gets cheaper when the wind blows.
The battery charges in strong sun, and discharges when a cloud passes.
That smooths out short swings, so jobs keep running instead of stopping for a checkpoint.
If the grid fails, the UPS bridges the first seconds until the generator takes over.
The commercial grid keeps priority work running, day or night.
When the wind blows, low cost wind power arrives through the grid.
Every source is chosen by cost and availability.
REPACSS. Making the computer follow the energy.
